subject: Modelling latent correlated variables in repeated-measures (aka. "within-subjects") design

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Modelling latent correlated variables in repeated-measures (aka. "within-subjects") design
parts:
Consider data-generating code as follows:

transformed data{
  vector[2] coef_means ; #intercept & effect means
  vector[2] coef_sds ; #intercept & effect sds
  corr_matrix[2] cor_mat ; #correlation btwn intercept & effect
  matrix[2,2] contrasts ; #contrasts to generate observed data
  #filling correlation matrix
  cor_mat[1,1] = 1 ;
  cor_mat[1,2] = .6 ;
  cor_mat[2,1] = .6 ;
  cor_mat[2,2] = 1 ;
  #fill means & sds
  coef_means[1] = 0 ; #intercept mean
  coef_means[2] = 0 ; #effect mean
  coef_sds[1] = 1 ; #intercept sd
  coef_sds[2] = 1 ; #effect sd
  #fill contrasts
  contrasts[1,1] = 1 ; #intercept
  contrasts[2,1] = 1 ; #intercept
  contrasts[1,2] = -1 ; #effect * -1
  contrasts[2,2] = 1 ; #effect * 1
}
parameters{
  vector[2] coefs ; #observed intercept & effect
}
model{
  #observed intercept & effect as multivariate normal
  coefs ~ multi_normal(
      coef_means
    , quad_form_diag( cor_mat , coef_sds )
  ) ;
}
generated quantities{
  matrix[2,3] dat ;
  dat[,1:2] = contrasts ; #save the contrasts used
  dat[,3] = contrasts * coefs ; #compute observed vals
}

saved as "make_data.stan" and used to generate data via R:

library(rstan)
nSubj = 100
#generate nSubj "subjects" of observed data
from_stan = rstan::stan(
  file = 'make_data.stan'
  , iter = nSubj*2
  , seed = 1
  , chains = 1
)
dat = rstan::extract(from_stan)$dat
dat = matrix(dat,ncol=3) #unwrap array
X = cbind(dat[,1],dat[,2]) #contrasts
Y = dat[,3] #observed values
subjID = rep(1:nSubj,times=2) #subject labels

Now, given this data (contrasts X and values Y for each of subject) I'd like to recover the original data-generating parameters (coef_means, coef_sds, cor), but I'm unsure how to structure the model. 

I know I can compute estimates of the coefs for each subject outside stan via lm:

est_coefs = matrix(NA,ncol=2,nrow=nSubj)
for(i in 1:nSubj){
  est_coefs[i,] = coef(lm(Y[subjID==i]~0+X[subjID==i,]))
}
data_for_stan = list(
  nSubj = nSubj
  , est_coefs = est_coefs
)

then run stan model like: 

data {
  int<lower=1> nSubj ;
  matrix[nSubj,2] est_coefs ;
}
parameters {
  vector[2] coef_means ;
  vector<lower=0>[2] coef_sds ;
  corr_matrix[2] cor_mat ;
}
model {
  coef_means ~ normal(0,1) ;
  coef_sds ~ weibull(2,1) ;
  cor_mat ~ lkj_corr(2) ;
  for(s in 1:nSubj){
    est_coefs[s,] ~ multi_normal( coef_means , quad_form_diag(cor_mat, coef_sds) ) ;
  }
}

But I'm wondering if there's a way to pass the X & Y & subjID data objects in directly rather than computing the coefficient estimates by hand in R first, not only because I'm lazy, but also because I'm eventually going to have more complicated coefficient designs and missing data at the observation level. 

Thoughts?

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: Modelling latent correlated variables in repeated-measures (aka. "within-subjects") design
parts:
Managed to work it out!

Given the data generated as previously described, one can compute the coefficients for each subject inside stan via:

data {
  int<lower=1> nSubj ;
  int<lower=1> nY ;
  int<lower=1> nX ;
  vector[nY] Y ;
  matrix[nY,nX] X ;
  int subjIndices[nSubj,2] ; #indices of start & finish of each subject in Y
}
transformed data{
  matrix[nSubj,nX] obs_coefs ;
  for(s in 1:nSubj){
    obs_coefs[s] = transpose(
      inverse(
        transpose( X[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]] )
        * X[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]]
      )
      * transpose( X[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]] )
      * Y[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]]
    ) ;
  }
}

So here would be the full model, with some scaling and unscaling of the coefficients for easy specification of weakly informed priors, but lacking any other optimizations:

data {
  int<lower=1> nSubj ;
  int<lower=1> nY ;
  int<lower=1> nX ;
  vector[nY] Y ;
  matrix[nY,nX] X ;
  int subjIndices[nSubj,2] ;
}
transformed data{
  matrix[nSubj,nX] obs_coefs ;
  matrix[nSubj,nX] scaled_coefs ;
  for(s in 1:nSubj){
    obs_coefs[s] = transpose(
      inverse(
        transpose( X[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]] )
        * X[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]]
      )
      * transpose( X[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]] )
      * Y[subjIndices[s,1]:subjIndices[s,2]]
    );
  }
  #scale the coefs for easy default priors
  for(i in 1:nX){
    scaled_coefs[,i] = (obs_coefs[,i] - mean(obs_coefs[,i])) / sd(obs_coefs[,i]) ;
  }
}
parameters {
  vector[nX] scaled_coef_means ;
  vector<lower=0>[nX] scaled_coef_sds ;
  corr_matrix[nX] cor_mat ;
}
model {
  scaled_coef_means ~ normal(0,1) ;
  scaled_coef_sds ~ weibull(2,1) ;
  cor_mat ~ lkj_corr(1) ;
  for(s in 1:nSubj){
    scaled_coefs[s,] ~ multi_normal( scaled_coef_means , quad_form_diag(cor_mat, scaled_coef_sds) ) ;
  }
}
generated quantities{
  vector[nX] coef_means ;
  for(i in 1:nX){
    coef_means[i] = scaled_coef_means[i]
      * sd(obs_coefs[,i])
      + mean(obs_coefs[,i])
      ;
  }
}
